intent: Make the mutation-testing claims in this session's four evidence files reproducible from the repo. They cited runs from a scratch directory that will not survive the session, leaving committed evidence pointing at something nobody could repeat.
scope: meta/scripts/mutate_shell.py - new: a spec-driven mutation runner
Non-goal: wiring this into pre-commit. It runs the full shell suite once per mutation, which is far too slow for a commit hook.
Non-goal: changing any subject or test; this only relocates and formalises checks already performed.
changes: Declared mutations in JSON with literal find/replace strings rather than sed expressions. The shell version escaped each pattern twice and used | as a field separator, which collided with || and silently reported six mutations as survivors when they had never been applied — a false negative in the exact tool meant to catch false negatives.

Counted a no-op (find matched nothing) as a failure rather than ignoring it. A stale spec entry otherwise stops testing its behaviour without ever saying so, which is the same silent-pass failure mode the tool exists to detect.
Restored the subject in a finally block, so an interrupted run cannot leave a deliberately broken file in the working tree.
Treated a timeout as killed: a mutation that makes the suite hang has still been detected by it.

verification.evidence: 18 killed, 0 not killed — matching the figure in monitor-coverage-backfill-2026-08-17.json.
Clean. The restore path returns each subject byte-for-byte; an earlier shell version left a mode-only diff behind, which is why this one uses copy2 and an unconditional finally.

Clean, including ruff, mypy and pylint. Ruff's autofixer removed a suppression during the first run; the tool was re-run afterwards and still reports 13 killed on backup_capture, so the autofix changed nothing behavioural.

verification.command: first conversion run of all four specs
verification.evidence: Reported 8 no-ops rather than silently passing, caused by the sed-to-literal conversion mangling escapes. Each was corrected against the actual source line and re-run. That the tool surfaced them rather than counting them as killed is the behaviour being relied on.

risks: The specs pin literal source text, so any edit to a mutated line makes its entry a no-op. That is reported loudly rather than passing quietly, but it does mean the specs need updating alongside the code they target.
This is not enforced by any hook. Nothing prevents a future shell library from being added with a coverage number and no mutation spec; the discipline remains a convention.
A full spec run takes minutes, since it executes the whole suite once per mutation. It is a deliberate, occasional check, not something to put in a tight loop.
rollback: git revert the commit. The four evidence files then cite mutation runs with no reproducible path, which is the state this commit exists to fix — prefer fixing forward.
After rollback, nothing else breaks: no hook, test or script references the tool.
